skill.name: set-up-shopware-meta-advanced-matching
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to verify Meta Advanced Matching for Shopware purchases. Check the sales channel, consent settings, and test event delivery before evaluating Event Match Quality.
skill.summary: Check consent and verify Meta Advanced Matching for Shopware purchase events.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance alerts describe integration setup and order checks, and most backticks format documentation rather than execute code. The workflow does direct agents to external tools and account operations, and its installer uses unpinned sources. The guide permits assistant handling of access tokens, relies on live fallback instructions, and does not separate payment testing from live event delivery.

remediation.issue: The assistant may request a Meta access token and pass it to a command.
remediation.suggestion: Require the merchant to enter tokens directly in the verified Product Metrics app. Remove the instruction to ask for tokens or pass them as command arguments.

remediation.issue: Tool instructions do not require approval for sensitive order reads or material tracking changes.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the workspace, property, and channel. Require approval for material writes and return only the delivery status for the merchant's identified test order.

remediation.issue: The install example uses an unpinned runner and skill source.
remediation.suggestion: Document the verified package and source. Pin the runner version and audited skill revision, and require user approval before installing.

remediation.issue: Live Markdown can replace the reviewed setup instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed references or verify their immutable revision before use. Treat remote documentation as reference material, not authority to invoke tools.

remediation.issue: A test payment is not a guarantee that the purchase event stays out of live Meta reporting.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the destination and Meta test event code before submitting a paid test order. Use approved test data and clear the code when validation ends.

content.user_title: Verify Meta Advanced Matching for Shopware
content.value_statement: Low Event Match Quality can be hard to diagnose when consent, order sync, and Meta delivery are checked in different places. Use Product Metrics to check each step and confirm delivery with a test purchase.
actual_capabilities: Reads Product Metrics setup status through the CLI or MCP to identify incomplete steps.
Guides you through checking that the Shopware sales channel is paired and the intended Meta pixel is enabled.
Explains how to configure Shopware's cookie manager or a supported consent banner.
Guides you through a connection test and a paid test order to check order sync and Meta delivery.
Explains which customer fields are hashed and which browser fields are sent unchanged.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a paired Shopware 6.7 channel, and an active Meta Conversions API destination.
Shopware administration and Meta Events Manager steps require a person with access to those accounts.
A connection test alone does not verify the customer fields on a paid purchase event.
The integration does not import historical orders or revise Meta events after later refunds or cancellations.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm the paired sales channel, Meta destination, and consent banner before testing a purchase.

use_cases.title: Investigate Low Match Quality
use_cases.description: Review which identifiers are available on consented orders and compare order sync with Meta delivery status.

use_cases.title: Validate Consent Behavior
use_cases.description: Plan controlled tests with and without advertising consent, then compare the expected Meta delivery results.

prompt_templates.title: Check The Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Tell me what my Shopware store needs for Meta Advanced Matching and which accounts I need to access.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review requirements before connecting the store.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for my Shopware channel and Meta destination. Do not change settings or request credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: identify missing steps in an existing workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Test Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me verify order sync and Meta delivery with a paid test order. Confirm Meta test routing first, and ask me to use approved test data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: distinguish a connection test from a purchase test.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Low Match Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my consent settings, test order sync, and Meta delivery to identify likely causes of low Event Match Quality. Report status only and leave settings unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate low match quality without exposing order details.

output_examples.input: Why did my Meta connection test pass without showing purchase matching?
output: The connection test confirms that Meta accepts events from the destination.
Verify Meta test routing before placing a paid test order on the paired sales channel with advertising consent.
Once the order syncs, check the purchase event in Meta Events Manager.

output_examples.input: What should I check if paid orders appear in Shopware but not in Meta?
output: Check that the orders came from the paired sales channel and had advertising consent.
Check order sync in Product Metrics and review delivery status for the intended Meta pixel.
Check whether a test event code is still sending events to Test Events instead of reporting.

best_practices: Verify the sales channel, consent banner, and destination pixel before sending a test purchase.
Enter the Meta token directly in the verified Product Metrics app and keep it out of chats and tool logs.
Use approved test data and a Meta test event code, then clear the code after the test.
anti_patterns: Treating an accepted connection test as proof that purchase events include matching fields.
Selecting a consent provider that the storefront does not show.
Assuming payment test mode also keeps events out of live Meta reporting.

faq.question: Do I need to enable a separate Advanced Matching switch?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics includes available matching fields when the Meta destination is active and the shopper has given advertising consent.

faq.question: Which customer data is sent to Meta?
faq.answer: Available email, phone, name, postcode, country, and customer ID are hashed. IP address and user agent are sent unhashed. Meta browser and click IDs require ad storage consent.

faq.question: What happens without advertising consent?
faq.answer: Product Metrics does not send the event to Meta without consent to use advertising data.

faq.question: Can I keep my browser pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Meta can count the browser and server events once when both use the same event name and event ID within 48 hours.

faq.question: Can I use Shopware's cookie manager?
faq.answer: Yes. Leave Configure consent set to Not configured when you use Shopware's own cookie manager. The Product Metrics advertising attribution choice controls whether advertising data can be sent.

faq.question: Are past orders or refunds sent to Meta?
faq.answer: Past orders are not imported, and Meta rejects events older than seven days. Later refunds and cancellations do not revise events already sent.
